import pandas as pd
df=pd.read_csv('data.csv')
cols=[c for c in df.columns if c!='outcome']
# count rows whose match on all-but-one column exists
from collections import Counter
hits=set()
for c in cols:
    key=df.drop(columns=[c]).astype(str).agg('|'.join,axis=1)
    d=key.duplicated(keep=False)
    hits|=set(df.index[d])
    print(c, d.sum())

# examples of near dups differing only in bmi or pedigree

cd /home/daytona/workspace && python3 -c "
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
df=pd.read_csv('data.csv')
k=df.copy(); k['bmi']=k.bmi.round(1); k['diabetes_pedigree']=k.diabetes_pedigree.round(2)
keep=~k.duplicated()
d=df[keep].reset_index(drop=True)
print('after dedupe', d.shape, d.outcome.mean().round(3))
tr,te=train_test_split(d,test_size=0.2,random_state=42,stratify=d.outcome)
tr.to_csv('train.csv',index=False); te.to_csv('test.csv',index=False)
print(tr.shape, te.shape, tr.outcome.mean().round(3), te.outcome.mean().round(3))
"
